hints.content: The total image width of $\maroonD{30.51} \text{ cm}$ includes the part of the image extending past the left edge of the page, the part on the page, and the part extending past the right edge of the page.

To find the width of the image that extends past the page edges, let's subtract the width of the page from the width of the image.

$\maroonD{30.51}-\blueD{21.59}=\purpleC{8.92}$

There will be $\purpleC{8.92}\,\text{cm}$ of the image extending past the edges of the page.

Since she wants to center the image on the page, the parts extending past each side must be equal.

The width extending past the left edge is equal to $\dfrac{1}{2}$ of the total width extending past the $2$ edges:

$\dfrac{ \purpleC{8.92} \,\text{cm} }{ 2 } = 4.46\,\text{ cm}$

There will also be $4.46\,\text{cm}$ of the width extending past the right edge of the page.

Horizontal positions to the *right* of the leftmost edge of the page are *positive*.

Since the horizontal position of the image will be $4.46\,\text{cm}$ to the *left* of the leftmost edge, the position will be *negative*.
Joelle should use a horizontal position of $-4.46\,\text{cm}$ for the left edge of the image.

question.content:
Joelle is working on a school report in a word processor. She wants to place an oversized image which is $30.51 \text{ cm}$ wide so that it appears centered on the page. The width of the page is $21.59 \text{ cm}$. In the program, horizontal positions to the right of the leftmost edge of the page are positive.

**What horizontal position for the left edge of the image should Joelle use to center the image?**

[[☃ numeric-input 1]] $\text{ cm}$

answers.message: This would be $4.46\,\text{cm}$ to the *right* of the leftmost edge, but the image is wider than the page, so it should start to the *left* of the edge.
